lessons.title: Comprehension: The school garden
lessons.programRef: MINEDUB primary school curriculum (English-speaking subsystem), Level III (Class 5) — English Language; to be checked against the official syllabus
lessons.author: CastBridge (AI draft)
lessons.source: Original writing following the Cameroonian curriculum; to be reviewed by a teacher
objectives: Understand the main ideas of a story.
Answer fact, meaning and opinion questions.
Find the lesson of the story.
reviewNotes: Syllabus references, scope and level of difficulty are to be checked against the official text; all facts, formulas and worked examples to be verified by a teacher before release.

blocks.md: Miss Fon's class decided to make a school garden. Every Friday the pupils dug the soil, planted beans and tomatoes, and watered them. At first, nothing grew and some pupils wanted to stop. Miss Fon said, 'A garden needs patience.' After three weeks, tiny green leaves came up. The pupils jumped for joy. At the end of the term, they sold the vegetables to parents and used the money to buy new books for the class library.

items.text: Characters: who is in the story?

blocks.caption: Questions to ask about a story.
blocks.alt: Four boxes: characters, setting, problem, ending.

blocks.title: Kinds of questions
blocks.md: **Literal questions** have the answer in the text (*What did the pupils plant?*). **Vocabulary questions** ask the meaning of a word (*'patience' means ...*). **Inference questions** ask what we can **work out** from clues (*How did the pupils feel after three weeks?*). **Opinion questions** ask what **you** think and why. Always **prove** your answer with words from the text.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Giving an inference when the text gives a fact.
- Writing an answer without proof from the text.
- Copying a whole sentence when only a few words are needed.
- Forgetting to answer both parts of a two-part question.

blocks.title: Example 1
steps: Find the sentence about planting: 'planted beans and tomatoes'.
blocks.answer: The pupils planted beans and tomatoes.

blocks.title: Example 2
blocks.statement: How did the pupils feel when the leaves appeared? How do you know?
steps: The text says they jumped for joy.
Jumping for joy shows they were very happy.
blocks.answer: They were very happy: they jumped for joy.

lessons.title: Comprehension: Saving water (an information text)
lessons.programRef: MINEDUB primary school curriculum (English-speaking subsystem), Level III (Class 5) — English Language; to be checked against the official syllabus
lessons.author: CastBridge (AI draft)
lessons.source: Original writing following the Cameroonian curriculum; to be reviewed by a teacher
objectives: Read an information text and find the main idea.
Write a short answer in your own words.
reviewNotes: Original text with common-sense advice; a health or water-agency worker could confirm the hygiene advice.
Syllabus references, scope and level of difficulty are to be checked against the official text; all facts, formulas and worked examples to be verified by a teacher before release.

blocks.md: Water is very important for life. We drink it, cook with it and wash with it. Farmers need water for their crops. Yet many people do not have clean water near their homes. We can save water in simple ways. Close the tap when you brush your teeth. Mend leaking pipes. Collect rain water in a drum and use it to water plants. Never throw rubbish into rivers, because dirty water can make people ill.

blocks.caption: The main idea and the key points of the text.
blocks.alt: Four boxes: the main idea that water is important, and three key points about closing the tap, mending leaks and keeping rivers clean.

blocks.title: Main idea and key points
blocks.md: The **main idea** is what the whole text is about, often in the first sentences: *water is important*. The **key points** are the important details that support it: ways of saving water. To find them, ask *What is the text about? What does it say about it?* Details such as examples can be left out in a short answer.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Copying many sentences instead of choosing the key ones.
- Mixing the main idea with one small detail.
- Adding information that is not in the text.
- Writing opinions as if the text said them.

blocks.title: Example 1
blocks.statement: What is the main idea of the text?
steps: Read the first sentences: 'Water is very important for life.'
The rest of the text explains why we need to save and protect it.
blocks.answer: Water is very important and we must save it and keep it clean.

blocks.title: Example 2
blocks.statement: Name two ways of saving water given in the text.
steps: Look for 'We can save water in simple ways.'
Close the tap when brushing teeth; mend leaking pipes (also: collect rain water).
blocks.answer: Close the tap; mend leaking pipes.

lessons.title: Summary writing
lessons.programRef: MINEDUB primary school curriculum (English-speaking subsystem), Level III (Class 5) — English Language; to be checked against the official syllabus
lessons.author: CastBridge (AI draft)
lessons.source: Original writing following the Cameroonian curriculum; to be reviewed by a teacher
objectives: Pick out the key points of a short text.
Write a short summary in your own words.
Keep to a given number of words.
reviewNotes: Word limits for summaries (for example 40 words) are not set here; the teacher can add them.
Syllabus references, scope and level of difficulty are to be checked against the official text; all facts, formulas and worked examples to be verified by a teacher before release.

blocks.title: Summary
blocks.md: A **summary** is a **short version** of a text. It keeps the **main points** and leaves out examples and small details. We write it in **our own words**, in full sentences, in the **same tense** as the text. It is much shorter than the passage.

items.text: Write them in your own words
Count the words: keep it short

blocks.caption: Four steps to write a summary.
blocks.alt: Four boxes: read the whole text, underline the key points, write them in your own words, count the words and keep it short.

blocks.md: Read this text. *Mama Ngo sells vegetables in the Mokolo market in Yaoundé. She wakes up at four o'clock and goes to the farm to buy tomatoes and cabbages. She arrives at the market at six. She sells until two in the afternoon. Then she goes home, cooks for her family and helps her children with their homework.*

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Copying whole sentences from the text.
- Adding your own opinions.
- Writing too long: a summary is a lot shorter than the text.
- Leaving out an important point, such as the work in the afternoon.

blocks.title: Example 1
blocks.statement: Find the key points of the text about Mama Ngo.
steps: Who: Mama Ngo, a vegetable seller. What: buys at the farm, sells at the market (4 a.m. to 2 p.m.).
After: goes home, cooks, helps her children.
blocks.answer: Mama Ngo buys vegetables at a farm, sells them in the market until two and then cares for her family.

blocks.title: Example 2
blocks.statement: Write a summary of the text in one sentence.
steps: Join the key points with and / then.
Mama Ngo buys vegetables at dawn, sells them in the market until two o'clock and then looks after her family.
blocks.answer: Mama Ngo buys vegetables at dawn, sells them in the market until two o'clock and then looks after her family.
